A.why: The bronze crown over a pale bone face is the clearest top-down read in the run and nails 'faintly regal grave guard'.
A.fix: Push the brown torso toward tarnished olive-bronze so the body stops reading as the leather family.

C.why: The black-and-bronze palette is distinct, and the round bronze grave-disc on the back is a fresh silhouette idea.
C.fix: Remove or bone-tint the stray white shoulder block that dominates the ARPG view, and dim the hot yellow eyes.

D.why: The bone-spike crown and moss-overgrowth patches tell the dug-up story best, but the brown base sits near leather and hide.
D.fix: Re-base the metal to tarnished bronze, unify the dark-green back with the front, and use fewer, larger moss patches.

B.why: A clean, distinct black-and-bronze build, but it reads as a generic dark knight with no strong idea or barrow story.
B.fix: Grow the helm prongs into a real barrow-king crest or crown, and add moss and bone.

F.why: A strong winged lamellar helm and a broad outline, but green-and-black with no bronze reads as samurai and fenscale-adjacent.
F.fix: Make the lamellar plates tarnished bronze with moss lacing, and bend the helm wings into burial-crown points.

E.why: An olive-green blob from above with no silhouette idea, too close to fenscale, and the yellow visor reads as hi-vis.
E.fix: Make tarnished bronze the dominant metal and commit to one silhouette idea such as a crested helm or a burial cape.

notes: Nobody owns tarnished bronze yet. A, C and D carry the barrow fantasy (crowns, bone, grave-disc, moss), but A and D lean brown toward leather, while E and F lean green toward fenscale. The winning direction is A's crown and bone face on C's black-and-bronze palette, plus D's moss patches.
